rounds.text: KRM Ayurveda Ltd is materially undervalued, backed by an intrinsic value estimate of Rs 383 per share against its current market price of Rs 262, leaving a healthy margin of safety of 31.7% [E34, E35]. The reverse DCF shows that the current market price only implies a 12.8% earnings growth rate, which sits comfortably below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E36]. Profitability and capital efficiency metrics are exceptionally strong, highlighted by a trailing ROCE of 35.3% and ROE of 29.0%, both drastically outperforming sector benchmarks of 12.7% and 11.94% respectively [E9, E10, E13, E54]. Growth has also accelerated dramatically in the short term, with trailing twelve-month sales compounding at 33% and profits surging by 66% alongside a widening operating margin of 30% [E15, E17, E20]. Furthermore, the company has successfully eliminated its debt entirely down to Rs 0 Cr from Rs 31 Cr a year earlier, achieving an immaculate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x while operating within a broader healthcare sector experiencing a strong macroeconomic tailwind score of +0.99 [E27, E28, E51]. Conceded: debtor days have increased from 56.5 to 81.6 days, working capital days have lengthened from 131 to 280 days, and the dividend yield remains at 0.00% [E4, E43, E44].

Despite reported profits, KRM Ayurveda Ltd suffers from a severe disconnect between earnings and actual cash generation, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.05x against reported profit for March 2026 [E23]. This is further underscored by free cash flow coming in at Rs 0 Cr and operating cash flow reaching a mere 29% of operating profit [E25, E26]. Working capital pressures are mounting aggressively, as evidenced by debtor days worsening from 56.5 to 81.6 days and total working capital days ballooning from 131 to 280 days [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% despite its profitability, failing to return capital to shareholders [E4, E42]. Operational quality also shows underlying volatility, with both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends labeled as inconsistent over recent periods [E21, E22]. Conceded: the company boasts zero debt, robust historical return metrics like a 3-year median ROE of 37%, and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 66% [E13, E17, E18, E28, E40].

While working capital days have indeed expanded, the underlying business is generating genuine momentum with a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 66% and sales surging 33% [E15, E17, E44]. Conceded: free cash flow sits at Rs 0 Cr and cash conversion against reported profit is low for March 2026 [E23, E25]. However, the company has completely eliminated its borrowings, wiping out Rs 31 Cr of debt down to zero, leaving it conservatively financed and fundamentally fortified [E28, E27]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% and operating margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E4, E21, E22]. Despite these bumps, profitability metrics remain exceptional, with ROCE at 35.3% and a 3-year median ROE of 37% [E12, E18]. Finally, the market price of Rs 262 provides a substantial 31.7% margin of safety relative to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 383, while the reverse DCF indicates that the current price only prices in a modest 12.8% earnings growth against a base case expectation of 18.0% [E2, E34, E35, E36].

Conceded: the company wiped out Rs 31 Cr of debt down to zero [E28] and trades below its DCF intrinsic value [E34]. However, the bull's reliance on trailing growth figures obscures a severe deterioration in fundamental cash generation and working capital health. Conceded: TTM profit and sales surged [E15, E17], but cash conversion for March 2026 stands at a dismal 0.05x, meaning profits are completely disconnected from actual cash in the bank [E23]. This is directly compounded by debtor days blowing out from 56.5 to 81.6 days and total working capital requirements nearly doubling from 131 days to an alarming 280 days [E43, E44]. Furthermore, free cash flow for March 2026 sits entirely at Rs 0 Cr [E25], exposing the reported earnings as paper profits trapped in uncollectible receivables rather than real liquidity. Operating margins remain explicitly inconsistent across both yearly and quarterly horizons [E21, E22], and the company returns nothing to shareholders with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] alongside a Price-to-Book ratio of 4.55x that outpaces the sector benchmark of 3.32x [E7].
